page: The Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare-metal server from the Bare Metal SSD family designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. The hardware is built upon the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9354P processor, delivering 32 physical cores and 64 threads running at a base clock of 3.25 GHz. Cache hierarchy details include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions span AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and hardware cryptography instructions such as AES and SHA-NI, which support vectorized computation and secure processing without virtualization overhead.

A defining characteristic of this configuration is its memory architecture, comprising 768 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding an allocation of 12 GB per virtual core. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier results in single-core stress testing and PassMark memory metrics, accompanied by strong multi-core processing and high cached memory throughput exceeding 5000 GB/s. For local persistence, the server includes a single 960 GB SSD. Because storage capacity is relatively compact given the 768 GB memory footprint, workloads demanding multi-terabyte on-disk persistence must rely on external network-attached storage. The platform does not incorporate a discrete graphics processing unit, reserving GPU-accelerated pipelines for other hardware tiers.

In terms of qualitative efficiency, the server balances high-speed DDR5 memory density against dedicated x86 CPU cores without the hypervisor tax of shared virtual instances. Evaluated benchmarks highlight strong throughput in Redis operations reaching over 91 million operations per second, fast software compilation, and effective CPU-based language model token generation. The system is suited for in-memory databases, extensive caching clusters, data engineering transformations, and high-concurrency enterprise services requiring predictable compute resources and massive RAM capacity.
description: The Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a dedicated bare-metal server configured for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9354P processor operating at 3.25 GHz, it provides 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs alongside advanced vector support including AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI. The system integrates 768 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 system memory, providing an extensive 12 GB of RAM per vCPU allocation, and includes a 960 GB local SSD. Benchmark testing places single-core execution and overall memory subsystem throughput in the top ten percent of evaluated systems, alongside strong multi-core and database processing scores. Lacking a discrete GPU and featuring modest local storage, the platform emphasizes core execution and primary memory density over massive local data persistence. It is suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise caching layers, compilation pipelines, and memory-bound analytics workloads.
